source.read_from: the bundled JavaScript of the pinned 2.0.18 release CLI (OpenCode Desktop's version-specific copy, which reports version 2.0.18 from /api/info), and the pinned OpenAPI fixture. For items (a) to (f) the source tree was not fetched: the bundle is minified, so each of those citations is a searchable identifier, not a line, and the release's tie to the tag's commit is the tag, not a byte comparison. Afterwards, with the operator's approval, the summary agent's use and the model calls that record no usage (item b) were read in the tag's own source, cited as sst/opencode tag v2.0.18 with file and line (E23 to E35).

evidence.says: the step's assistant message gets time.completed, finish, cost and tokens in one edit, when the step ends; it was created at session.step.started with time.created, the model and no tokens
a failed step also gets time.completed, finish (default error) and error, and cost and tokens only when the failure carries them

the session's totals live on its own row and grow by addition only (the function before it, Pc: cost = cost + usage.cost, tokens_input = tokens_input + usage.tokens.input, and so on), keyed by the event's own sessionID: no roll-up from child sessions

a step's end updates its message, then adds its usage to the session's totals; a failed step adds usage only when cost and tokens are present; session.usage.recorded adds to the totals (yield*e.project(hd,(i)=>Pc(r,i.data.sessionID,i.data)))
the bus runs a durable event's projectors inside the publish's l.transaction(...,{behavior:"immediate"}), so a step's message and its session's totals commit together
auxiliary usage (title and compaction) is its own durable event; the message projector ignores it ("session.usage.recorded":()=>F), so title usage is on no message
a compaction publishes session.usage.recorded (source compaction) first and session.compaction.ended (model: the context's model ref, tokens, cost) after: two transactions, the totals first

the title call uses the title agent's model when configured, else the session provider's small model (i.small(providerID)) with a none, minimal or low variant; SessionTitle.attempt records its usage as session.usage.recorded source title
a subagent runs in a child session (parentID) on the explicit model, else the subagent's own model, else the parent session's model; its usage goes to the child's own totals

an interrupted or failed step carries usage only if the provider's finish (with usage) arrived; otherwise the message ends with time.completed, finish error and no tokens, and the totals do not move: what the call consumed is unrecorded
a committed revert deletes the session's messages from the boundary on (and its pending inputs) and never touches the totals

a fork is a new root session (parent_id null, fork_session_id the source) with cost and every token column 0, holding copies (new ids, original time_created) of the source's finished messages up to the boundary

evidence.identifier: AND (session.fork_session_id IS NULL OR message.time_created >= session.time_created)
evidence.says: OpenCode's own usage statistics exclude a fork's copies by their creation time before the fork's

OpenCode's own finished-message rule (session export, and the fork copy's SQL): an assistant message is finished when it has time.completed, a compaction or shell message when its status is not running
a compaction's end completes its message and advances the instruction epoch (UE=u("InstructionState.advanceEpoch")): no message is deleted and the totals are not lowered

session.list orders and anchors its cursor on time.updated and id, and returns a next cursor whenever a page has items; session.messages refuses a cursor combined with order ("Cursor cannot be combined with order"), defaults to order desc, and its cursor carries only the anchor's id, the order and the direction (see E22 for a cursor whose anchor is gone)

SessionStore.messages looks the cursor's anchor id up among the session's messages and, when it is gone (a revert deleted it), returns an empty page, with no next cursor, for good; otherwise it pages by position (seq) after the anchor, filtered by type

a completed compaction has id, time.created, status, reason, summary, recent and optional model, tokens, cost, providerContext; a failed one has error and optional tokens and cost but no model; a running one has no tokens; an assistant message's time has created, completed and streamed, and it may carry retry {attempt, at, error}
a deleted session's row goes, with its messages: the session vanishes from the list

the summary agent is defined (hidden, no default model) and nothing else in the bundle names it; the tag's source confirms it (E23 to E27); and the compaction call runs on the context's model (SessionContext.load resolves the session's model)

AEW's projection pins the title, summary and compaction agents to the run's model and sets no compaction.auto: C1's CC2 (auto off for bounded workers) is not merged, so workers, the Lead and R keep OpenCode's default (auto on)
session.active lists the sessions with an execution running
the summary agent is defined here (hidden, primary, the PROMPT_SUMMARY system text, every action denied, no model); in the tag's source, outside tests, nothing else names the agent or its prompt
a hidden agent is never selected as a session's default or fallback agent
the subagent tool offers the model only agents that are neither primary nor hidden, so a model cannot start the summary agent as a subagent
an agent named explicitly (a session created with it, or switched to it) is returned even when hidden: the summary agent runs only when a client names it, or a configured command does (E32)

a session's steps run on the session's own model, whatever its agent; so a session running the summary agent records ordinary steps (assistant messages with time.completed and tokens, added to the totals, E1 and E4), which the meter counts

session generation runs one model call from the session's context with the session's agent and model, writes no message and publishes no session.usage.recorded: its usage goes only to a log line ("session generation usage diagnostic"), so it reaches neither a message nor Session.Info.tokens
session generation is served as POST /api/session/:sessionID/generate (handler: packages/server/src/handlers/session.ts:587-590); its callers are listed in E34 and E35

evidence.identifier: const response = yield* llm.generate(LLM.request({ model: resolved.model, prompt: input.prompt })).pipe(
evidence.says: a stateless generation on the requested or the default model, outside any session, served as POST /api/experimental/generate (packages/protocol/src/groups/generate.ts:8; handler packages/server/src/handlers/generate.ts:17-19) and to plugins (E35); it records no usage anywhere

the internal plugin opencode.warming (registered at packages/core/src/plugin/internal.ts:249) calls session generation (:49-50) only when the configuration sets `warming` (off by default, :20-21), and only for root sessions (a session with a parentID is skipped, :61); by default every 4 minutes for 30 minutes after a turn, both configurable (`interval`, `duration`, :9-13, :22); those calls record no usage (E28)

a configured command that names an agent runs it either as a subtask in a new child session (:98-106) or by switching the invoking session's agent, and its model when one is given (:124-128); either way its calls are ordinary steps on that session's model

for the github-copilot provider, when the title agent has no model, the title is made by the plugin's own /chat/completions call, and the title path returns that result before recording usage (packages/core/src/session/title.ts:73); title and compaction usage is recorded only when the provider reported it (title.ts:57-64; packages/core/src/session/compaction.ts:435-443, 556-563, 610-618)

the first-party `/btw` side question calls session generation over HTTP: in the TUI, a built-in plugin (packages/tui/src/plugin/builtins.ts:2) with the slash command `btw`, and in the app (packages/app/src/session/btw/model.ts:67); it is on by default and user-initiated

the plugin host gives every plugin session generation (:535) and the stateless generation (:272), also through the promise adapter (packages/plugin/src/promise/adapter.ts:340, :586); with the server handlers (E29, E30), the warming plugin (E31) and `/btw` (E34), these are all the callers of both entry points in the tag

findings.says: An assistant message is created at step start with time.created and its model, and no tokens. It gets time.completed with finish and its tokens when the step ends, or time.completed, finish error, error (and tokens only if usage was reported) when it fails. time.completed marks every recorded call; finish and error are never set without it, so the R3-m1 rule reduces to time.completed on 2.0.18.

Session.Info.tokens and cost are that session's own: its steps, plus its title and compaction calls through session.usage.recorded. Child sessions are never included. Defaults: title on the title agent's model, else the provider's small model; compaction on the session's model; a subagent on its explicit, own or parent's model. AEW pins title, summary and compaction to the run's model.

2.0.18 never calls the summary agent by itself: it is defined (hidden, primary, no model) and nothing outside tests names it; a hidden agent is never a default and is never offered to the model as a subagent. It runs only when a client names it (creating or switching a session to it) or a configured command names it (as a subtask in a child session, or by switching the session). Its steps are then ordinary steps on that session's model, on assistant messages the meter counts and in the session's totals. AEW's projection pins it to the run's model. Session generation, with any agent, records nothing (b-unrecorded).

Some model calls record no usage in 2.0.18, so no message and no total carries them and the meter cannot see them: session generation, whose callers are POST /api/session/:sessionID/generate, the first-party `/btw` side question in the TUI and the app (on by default, user-initiated), the plugin host's session.generate, and the `warming` plugin (when the configuration sets `warming`, off by default, root sessions only); the stateless generation, whose callers are POST /api/experimental/generate and the plugin host's generate.text; the github-copilot utility title (only when the title agent has no model); title and compaction calls whose provider reported no usage; and an interrupted step before the provider's finish (E10). Their usage is outside every live figure; the provider reconciliation (Q7 v0.3.1 §9.1) is the backstop.

Tokens move only when a call ends: the message and the totals are written at step end (or failure with usage, or session.usage.recorded), never during streaming. An interrupted call without the provider's finish is recorded with time.completed, finish error and no tokens, and the totals do not move: what it consumed is billed and unrecorded (A1).

Nothing lowers a session's totals. Compaction adds usage and removes no message. A committed revert deletes messages from its boundary on and keeps the totals; a message cursor anchored on a deleted message then returns an empty page for good (E22), so the meter, when the totals moved and the anchor is gone, reads the session again from the start and skips what it passed already. A fork is a new session with zero totals holding copies of the source's finished messages (created before the fork): the meter counts only a fork's messages created at or after the fork, as OpenCode's own statistics do. Deleting a session removes it from the list. C1's CC2 is not merged, so compaction stays on by default everywhere.

A step's message (time.completed, tokens) and its session's totals are written by one durable event's projectors in one SQLite transaction, message first: a reader never sees one without the other, but the list and a message page are separate reads, so messages can run ahead of the totals read earlier (skew, not a breach). A compaction's totals are committed before its message completes; a title's only ever reach the totals.

A completed compaction message carries status completed, reason, summary, recent and optional model, tokens and cost (no time.completed: its status marks it finished); a failed one has error and optional tokens and cost but no model. The auxiliary defaults are as in (b).

event_payloads: The pinned OpenAPI types events as an opaque string, so this fixture is the only pin on event payloads; the meter relies on none.

cases.name: a step's message and totals land together
title usage reaches the totals on no message, priced on the pinned model
without a proven pin, the title's usage prices nothing
a compaction's totals lead its message, and count once
an interrupted call ends with no usage and never stalls the cursor
a child session's totals are its own and are never counted twice
a session on another model is its own partition
a fork's copies of finished messages are never counted again
a revert removes messages but never the totals
a revert of the cursor's anchor, then more calls, are counted once each
a failed compaction has no model: its usage is left to the totals
totals written lower than seen are flagged and never lower the figure
